This integration brings your **Last.fm listening** into Gladys: what you are listening to right now, your scrobbles, scenes that react to the music, and three dashboard widgets.

Last.fm records ("scrobbles") every track played on Spotify, Deezer, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Tidal, Plex, Sonos and many more players. Whatever the player: if your listening reaches your Last.fm profile, Gladys sees it.

> Community integration, not affiliated with Last.fm.

## Setup

### 1. Create an API key (free)

1. Sign in to Last.fm, then open [Create an API account](https://www.last.fm/api/account/create).
2. Fill in an application name (e.g. "Gladys") and a description. The **callback URL can stay empty**.
3. Last.fm shows an **API key** (32 characters) and a **shared secret**. Find them again at any time in [My API accounts](https://www.last.fm/api/accounts).

### 2. Fill in the integration

| Field                  | Purpose                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **API key**            | required                                                                 |
| **Shared secret**      | only to link an account (love tracks from Gladys)                        |
| **Profiles to follow** | Last.fm usernames separated by commas (10 at most): yours, a relative's… |
| **Refresh interval**   | 30 seconds by default (15 to 300): this is how fast the scenes react     |

Save. The **Test the connection** button checks the key and reads every profile.

A profile that **hides its recent listening** (Last.fm privacy settings) cannot be followed: Last.fm refuses to share it.

### 3. Add the devices

On the **Discovery** tab, each followed profile shows up as a "Last.fm – _name_" device. Add it and put it in a room. Widgets and scenes work without a device too, but picking a profile in their settings goes through the device list.

### 4. Link your account (optional)

Only to **love or unlove** tracks from Gladys (widget button, scene actions):

1. fill in the **shared secret** and save;
2. click **Connect**: a Last.fm page opens;
3. click **Yes, allow access**. Gladys notices within a few seconds: the configuration screen reads "account _name_ linked".

Nothing else is needed: no redirect URL to declare. The page stays valid 15 minutes; past that, click Connect again.

To unlink: the **Unlink the account** button, and optionally revoke the access in your Last.fm settings (Applications).

## The device of a profile

| Feature                   | Value                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Listening**             | 1 while a track is playing, 0 otherwise                       |
| **Current or last track** | "Artist – Track"; keeps the last track once listening stopped |
| **Scrobbles today**       | since midnight, in the Gladys time zone                       |
| **Total scrobbles**       | since the account was created                                 |

History is kept: the dashboard "Chart" box shows your week of listening, and the usual scenes on a device value work ("more than 100 scrobbles today"…).

## Scene triggers

In the scene editor, under **Last.fm**:

| Trigger                        | Fires when…                                                   | Filters         |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| **Last.fm: new track**         | a profile starts playing a track                              | profile, artist |
| **Last.fm: listening started** | a profile starts listening after a pause                      | profile         |
| **Last.fm: listening stopped** | nothing has been playing for two checks in a row              | profile         |
| **Last.fm: track loved**       | a profile loves a track (on Last.fm or in a connected player) | profile, artist |

Passed on to the scene actions: username, artist, track, album, loved, Last.fm link, and a ready-to-send **summary**; for "listening stopped", the session length (minutes) and the number of tracks played.

Examples:

- **Listening started** → dim the living room and power the amplifier on;
- **Listening stopped** → power the amplifier off;
- **New track**, artist "Daft Punk" → disco lights.

Good to know:

- The **Artist** filter compares the name **exactly** as Last.fm spells it, case included ("Daft Punk", not "daft punk").
- Last.fm pushes nothing: the integration reads the profiles every 30 seconds by default, so a scene reacts within a few seconds to half a minute.
- When the integration starts, a session already in progress does not fire "Listening started"; only the next track counts.
- The same track played twice in a row counts once (Last.fm gives no way to tell the two plays apart).

## Scene actions

| Action                            | Result                                                                          |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Last.fm: what is playing**      | listening (yes/no), artist, track, album, loved, link, time played, summary     |
| **Last.fm: listening statistics** | scrobbles today and in total, top artist / album / track over a period, summary |
| **Last.fm: love a track**         | adds a track to the loved tracks of the linked account                          |
| **Last.fm: unlove a track**       | removes it                                                                      |

To love or unlove: leave **artist and track empty** to target the track playing now (or the last one played) on the linked account, or fill them in (scene variables accepted). Both actions need a linked account.

## Dashboard widgets

| Widget                    | Content                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Last.fm now playing**   | cover, track, artist and album, scrobbles today and in total, status, **Love** button (linked account), link |
| **Last.fm recent tracks** | the latest tracks with their covers; the track playing now and the loved ones are badged                     |
| **Last.fm top charts**    | top artists, albums (as a cover grid) or tracks over 7 days, 1, 3, 6 or 12 months, or all time               |

Each widget is set to a profile (empty = the first followed profile). The "now playing" widget refreshes as soon as a new track starts.

Last.fm has not served artist pictures since 2019: the top artists show without images.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                             | Likely cause                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Last.fm refuses the API key"       | key miscopied, or a wrong shared secret when linking                             |
| A profile is missing from Discovery | the username does not exist (see the integration logs)                           |
| "hides their recent listening"      | the profile enabled the matching privacy option on Last.fm                       |
| Nothing happens while listening     | the player does not scrobble: check that the track shows on your Last.fm profile |
| The Connect button fails            | shared secret missing: fill it in and save before clicking                       |

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Last.fm in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Last.fm API key | `section` | Nein | Last.fm records what you listen to on Spotify, Deezer, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Plex and many more. Reading your listening needs a free API key: create an API account on Last.fm (any application name; the callback URL can stay empty), then copy its API key and shared secret below. |
| API key | `secret` | Ja | 32 characters. |
| Shared secret | `secret` | Nein | Only needed to link an account (to love tracks). |
| Profiles to follow | `string` | Ja | Last.fm usernames, separated by commas (10 at most). Each one becomes a device on the Discovery screen. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | Nein | How often the profiles are read, between 15 and 300 seconds. Last.fm has no push: this is the delay of the scenes. |
| Link your account (optional) | `section` | Nein | Only needed to love or unlove tracks from Gladys (widget button, scene actions). Fill in the shared secret and save first, then click Connect and approve the access on the Last.fm page that opens. Gladys detects the approval within a few seconds. |
| Last.fm account | `account_link` | Nein |  |

## So installierst du Last.fm in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Last.fm erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/william-de71/gladys-lastfm:1.0.0`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-lastfm](https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-lastfm).

Last.fm benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.1`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Last.fm ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [William-De71](https://github.com/William-De71) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
